title: Microfront LLM integration patterns and guardrails (draft)
summary: Working draft: recommended SDK integration patterns for microfrontends that embed LLM features (autocompletion, assistant panels, constrained code generation). Focus on lightweight adapters, telemetry boundaries, failure modes, and a 5‑step quickstart for product teams.
audience: frontend engineers, sdk integrators, platform engineers, solutions engineers
objective: Provide a concise, repeatable onramp for teams adding Redwood-powered LLM features into microfrontends with minimal bundle impact and predictable telemetry and cost profiles.
context_and_motivation: We keep seeing small product teams embed LLM features directly into microfronts (chat drawer, inline completions, code helpers) and repeatedly run into the same problems: oversized client bundles, inconsistent telemetry, token cost surprises, and fragile fallbacks. This doc captures patterns we've validated in internal pilots and recommends a guarded quickstart that balances UX and production safety.
principles: 1) Thin client, fat server: keep heavy logic and model routing on the platform side. 2) Instrument early: telemetry + sample prompts before launch. 3) Fail predictable: deterministic fallbacks and safe-mode UX. 4) Cost-aware defaults: conservative timeouts, batching, and preview tokens. 5) Developer ergonomics: adapter contracts and small SDK surface for microfronts.
pattern_overview: High-level patterns we propose: (A) Adapter surface: a small JS shim (0.5-3 KB gz) per microfront that exposes generate/chat/embed helper methods and normalizes errors/latency; (B) Edge-proxy routing: route requests through a per-product edge proxy that applies cost policies and prefix caching; (C) Interaction guards: client-side debounce + length caps + optimistic UI; (D) Telemetry fences: send minimal token counts and intent labels from client, full prompt payloads only from server side for eval; (E) Offline dev stubs: local stub runner that mimics Redwood responses for dev.
adapter_contract_examples:
Adapter API (minimal):
- init({apiKey, productId, env})
- suggest(text, opts) -> Promise<{text, tokensUsed, meta}>
- chat.append(message) / chat.finish()
- on('latency', cb)
Notes: adapter should never expose raw API keys. Keys are short-lived client tokens minted by backend. Adapter should attach productId and flowId to every call for telemetry.
quickstart_5_step:
Quickstart (5 steps) - for a single microfront (chat drawer / input completion):
1) Install adapter package from sdk registry (yarn add @redwood/mini-adapter).
2) Create backend token endpoint (mint short-lived token with productId + role). See sample at /api/redwood/token (link in linked_artifacts).
3) Replace direct SDK calls with adapter.suggest() and implement on('error') to show safe-mode UI.
4) Enable telemetry fences: client sends only: event, flowId, productId, input_length, latency_estimate. Server side correlates tokens.
5) Launch behind feature flag + canary to 5% with strict quota and alerts (see rollout-checklist below).
Notes: include code snippet in real doc; this draft sketches the flow.
telemetry_and_metrics:
Recommended metrics to collect pre-launch and for ongoing ops:
- client_attempts_per_flow (counts)
- median_latency_ms (p95, p99)
- tokens_consumed_per_request (derived server-side)
- cost_per_active_user (weekly)
- fallback_rate (client-side triggers)
- prompt_regression_rate (QA eval hooks)
Implementation note: clients send only hashed flowId and lightweight counts. Full prompt payloads should be stored server-side only for customers who opt-in; default is opt-out.
failure_modes_and_fallbacks: Common failure modes: network blips, rate-limiting, model hallucination, high token cost. Recommended fallback ladder: 1) transient: simple retry with jitter + cached prefix; 2) degraded UX: show trimmed suggestion (max 40 tokens) using cached_completion; 3) safe-mode: disable generation and show canned help text; 4) emergency: circuit-breaker opens and route to a lower-cost model or static content. For hallucinations, attach detection label in server evals and trigger immediate human review if in prod canary.
security_and_privacy_guidance: - Never put full prompt blobs in client telemetry. - Use per-product scoped tokens with short TTLs. - For regulated customers consider server-only mode (no client direct calls). - PII scrubbing: client should run a client-side regex scrubber for obvious PII before sending unless product requires raw text for feature (then must be opt-in and logged).
edge_cases_and_notes_to_self:
- Multi-tenant microfronts: ensure productId in token scope.
- Offline prefetching: avoid prefetching large completions when on slow networks.
- Accessibility: keep fallback flows keyboard-navigable.
- Mobile constraints: include a tiny mobile adapter variant with smaller default token caps.
Notes to self: prototype mobile adapter by March sprint; pair with Marco for token mint endpoint template.
rollout_checklist:
Rollout gating checklist (give to product ops before enabling):
- [ ] Feature flag created (ff-llm-<product>)
- [ ] Quota configured (max tokens/day per UID)
- [ ] Alerts: cost spike, p95 latency > threshold, fallback_rate > 2%
- [ ] Canary plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days with manual stop gates
- [ ] Instrumentation: correlation id present in logs for every call
- [ ] Post-launch review scheduled (7 days)
- [ ] UX fallback copy approved by content team
Responsible: Solutions Eng + Platform infra.
open_questions:
1) Should we expose a separate 'preview' model with cheaper pricing for inline suggestions? (depends on pricing tiers)
2) How do we standardize client-side PII scrubbing rules across products? (legal input needed)
3) Is the short-lived token flow acceptable latency-wise for mobile cold starts? (need real perf numbers)
4) Should SDK expose automatic debounce or leave to app code? Current preference: keep opt-in automatic with conservative defaults.
